frequency_citation.text: Medicare pays for a screening BMM once every 2 years (at least 23 months have passed since the month the last covered BMM was performed).

hcpcs_citation.text: HCPCS procedure codes for bone mass measurement
hcpcs_citation.note: Codes mentioned in CMS coding guidelines, not explicit in main policy text

eligible_conditions: Estrogen-deficient women at clinical risk for osteoporosis
Individuals with vertebral abnormalities indicative of osteoporosis/osteopenia/fracture
Individuals receiving/expecting glucocorticoid therapy ≥5mg prednisone/day for >3 months
Individuals being monitored for FDA-approved osteoporosis drug therapy response

conditions_citation.text: To be covered, a beneficiary must meet at least one of the five conditions listed below: 1. A woman who has been determined by the physician or qualified nonphysician practitioner treating her to be estrogen-deficient...

exclusions_citation.text: The following BMMs are noncovered under Medicare because they are not considered reasonable and necessary under section 1862(a)(1)(A) of the Act. • Single photon absorptiometry (effective January 1, 2007). • Dual photon absorptiometry (established in 1983).

special_rules: More frequent BMMs allowed when medically necessary (e.g., monitoring glucocorticoid therapy)
Confirmatory BMM must use dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry if initial was not DEXA
Monitoring drug therapy response must use DEXA (axial skeleton)

gold_compiled_edit.filter_logic: HCPCS_Cd IN ('77080', '77081') AND Tot_Benes >= 11 AND (Tot_Srvcs / Tot_Benes) > 0.7826

validation_notes.frequency_interpretation: Policy says 'once every 2 years (at least 23 months)'. We interpret this as 23-month minimum interval, which translates to ~0.52 services/beneficiary/year.
validation_notes.threshold_rationale: 1.5x multiplier provides buffer for legitimate variation while catching outliers
validation_notes.hcpcs_source: HCPCS codes 77080/77081 are standard for bone density measurement but not explicitly listed in policy text - sourced from CMS coding guidelines
limitations: Provider-level utilization is aggregated - cannot detect per-beneficiary violations
Cannot verify eligible conditions (estrogen-deficient, etc.) from claims data alone
Does not account for 'medically necessary' exceptions

metadata.methodology: Manual extraction from official CMS NCD text with character-level citation tracking
